From the goal-line technology introduced at the 2014 Brazil World Cup, to VAR and semi-automated offside technology in 2018 and 2022 respectively, and AI-assisted referee cameras at this year's tournament, FIFA has introduced innovations four tournaments in a row. During live broadcasts, global audiences have more exposure to sponsors of refereeing technology, while computer-aided decisions frequently become the focal point of match controversies. However, FIFA has even bigger ambitions for introducing technology into the game. This year's tournament has further cemented the role of "smart football" — the match ball can detect data up to 500 times per second, including goal rotation frequency, shot force, and flight speed.

FIFA AI Pro system powered by Lenovo technology

The newly introduced FIFA AI Pro system, powered by Lenovo technology, can generate virtual models of players through artificial intelligence. In Hong Kong, Lenovo partnered with the Jockey Club to showcase the system at Happy Valley, and even invited England football legend David Beckham to Hong Kong for promotional purposes. Lenovo stated that the system can integrate and instantly analyse up to 2,000 data points.

The Jockey Club is the only organisation in Hong Kong that legally offers World Cup betting, and the collaboration between the two parties reveals the potential gambling applications of the data. This year's tournament is estimated to directly generate up to 90 petabytes of data — 45 times that of the previous edition. Combined with data from the internet, social media, and match predictions, the figure reaches 2 exabytes, equivalent to streaming World Cup matches in 4K resolution for 90,000 years.

FIFA has in recent years established its own football data ecosystem, officially explaining that high technology helps teams, players, and fans reinterpret and analyse match tactics. On the other hand, FIFA earlier this year sold global betting data and exclusive betting streaming distribution rights for the first time, meaning big data including this World Cup will be given betting applications, opening up new revenue streams.

Before the World Cup kicked off, ADIPredictStreet, a prediction market institution established just months ago and backed by the Abu Dhabi royal family, became FIFA's first top-level partner of its kind with a deal worth US$150 million. This year's tournament demonstrates that technology not only has the power to determine match results on the pitch, but is also enough to influence the way people engage off the pitch. Yet the only party with influence over both is FIFA, and ensuring no conflict of interest is involved will be a major challenge.

Citing rules to overturn decision FIFA accused of overstepping the mark

To further expand revenue streams, increasing the population base is undoubtedly the way forward for FIFA. Since the 2018 Russia World Cup, FIFA has reformed its existing commercial sponsorship hierarchy, introducing regional sponsors for the first time, dividing the world into five major regions. This year has seen the addition of a host city sponsorship programme for the first time. Both reflect FIFA's need to more precisely target the commercial interests represented by fans around the world, while also breaking away from the traditional dominance of established footballing nations at the World Cup.

Host nation the United States is not a traditional football powerhouse. In the round-of-32 knockout match against Bosnia, their key striker Balogun received a red card. US President Trump subsequently admitted to calling FIFA president Infantino to demand a review of the decision. FIFA ultimately cited regulations to allow Balogun to return to play — the first such case since the 1962 Chile World Cup. The incident drew widespread criticism, with UEFA unusually issuing a statement describing FIFA's move as "crossing the red line".

Just as Balogun was sent off, sitting in the VIP area of the stands were US Commerce Secretary Lutnick and Infantino. Sources revealed that the two had dined together in early June but kept it private, and the suspension incident was actually coordinated between them behind the scenes. Regional sponsors include numerous American companies, and Balogun started in the round-of-16 match against Belgium. The US eventually was eliminated, but over 50 million people across the country watched the match, still setting an all-time record for football viewership in the United States.

The provision of FIFA's Code of Ethics that was cited has previously been invoked in the case of Cristiano Ronaldo, to prevent him from missing the first two matches of this World Cup. Ronaldo is the most-followed person globally on Instagram, and his commercial value to the tournament is beyond doubt. His current Saudi club Al Nassr is mainly owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), which is also the official sponsor for North America and Asia at this World Cup, and is a key driver of the country's sports commercialisation and its bid to host the World Cup.

Making a name on the map — a World Cup "belonging to the whole world"

As World Cup fever reaches almost every corner of the globe, fans from different places hope that one day their teams will qualify for the finals, or even go further. With each national federation holding equal voting rights, FIFA's management needs to consider the interests of all member nations, but the system has also become a breeding ground for corruption. For example, the 2015 FIFA corruption scandal uncovered bribery involving CONCACAF and CONMEBOL in an attempt to influence the host selection process. These federations were also implicated in the case involving a former Fox executive bribing over broadcast rights, but on the eve of this World Cup, a federal judge dismissed the charges on the grounds that the case "did not align with the current policy priorities of the Trump administration." Fox also holds the US broadcast rights for this World Cup.

At the same time, the representation ratio of the continents at the World Cup has already changed, and opportunities for countries outside Europe to participate in this top-tier tournament are on the rise.
